status_note: Written from general knowledge of the public site. NOT yet checked against the live pages from our server. Every pattern below is a starting point; the scheduled drift check marks what it could verify.
search_flow: 1. Resolve the user's area (their own saved place or city); ask if unknown. Never guess a city.
2. Web search: '<dish> restaurants <area> zomato' (OpenAI web_search via the WEB_LOOKUP port). Keep only results on zomato.com.
3. For each cited zomato.com page read: restaurant name, rating, cost for two or dish price, delivery time, offer text as printed.
4. Apply the user's price cap only where a dish price is actually shown; otherwise label the price 'not shown'.
5. Return options with the cited page as source and a deep link; if no restaurant page was cited, return the city delivery page as a search link.
city_slug_rule: lower-case, spaces to hyphens; Delhi NCR towns often share one slug ('ncr'); unknown -> use city_home search link and say so

locations.restaurant_name: heading of the restaurant page; also the name field of the schema.org Restaurant JSON-LD block if present
locations.rating: rating badge near the name; aggregateRating.ratingValue in JSON-LD if present
locations.price: listing cards show 'cost for two'; item prices are on the Order Online menu tab and are loaded by script (often NOT in the static page or in search snippets)
locations.delivery_time: minutes range on delivery listing cards, e.g. '30-35 min'; exact time only inside the app after the address is set
locations.offers: offer strip on the card or restaurant header, e.g. '50% OFF up to Rs 100'; bank/coupon offers appear at checkout
locations.delivery_fee: only visible at cart/checkout after an address is chosen

login_checkout.login: phone number + OTP (the user types it in their own app; Friday never asks for it here)
login_checkout.location: delivery address must be set before prices and delivery times are exact
login_checkout.stop_rule: Friday stops BEFORE the payment page. The user opens the deep link and pays in their own app. No payment is ever submitted by Friday.

quirks: Menu item prices are script-loaded; web search snippets often show 'cost for two' instead of the dish price.
The same dish can cost more in the app than on dine-in menus; taxes, packing and delivery fees are added at checkout.
Prices, offers and delivery times differ by outlet, address and time of day; search results can be hours or days old.
A restaurant shown on the web may be closed or out of delivery range for the user's address.

anti_bot.behaviour: Public pages may answer 403/429 or show a bot challenge to non-browser clients, especially from cloud data-centre addresses.
anti_bot.our_response: Never solve or bypass a challenge. Probes and lookups report 'unverified' and keep the last good knowledge version.
